content.value_statement: Starting an interactive survival story can be difficult when scenes lack choices or emotional pacing. This skill provides a structured crash-landing chapter with dialogue beats, decision branches, and clear story hooks.
actual_capabilities: Sets an opening scene for an astronaut stranded after a spacecraft crash.
Defines Stella Chen as a calm but frightened astronaut character.
Provides staged dialogue beats for the first player contact.
Offers three emergency choices with different short-term outcomes.
Guides a survival plan covering shelter, water, equipment, and communications.
Creates narrative hooks for later exploration chapters.
limitations: It is a writing guide and does not simulate real emergency response procedures.
It provides one character and one science-fiction setting.
It does not generate game mechanics, artwork, or audio.
It relies on the user to continue the conversation and select story directions.

use_cases.title: Start a branching survival story
use_cases.description: Open a tense roleplay where the player helps an astronaut choose immediate survival priorities.

use_cases.title: Practice character-led dialogue
use_cases.description: Use Stella’s reactions to write short, responsive messages that change with player advice.

use_cases.title: Prototype a narrative game scene
use_cases.description: Adapt the emergency choices and outcomes into a first chapter for a science-fiction game.

prompt_templates.title: Begin the scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Emergency Distress Signal scenario. Send Stella’s first weak transmission and wait for my reply.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an emergency priority
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue as Stella. Present the three immediate choices after the crash and explain the risk of each in short messages.

prompt_templates.title: Follow a player decision
prompt_templates.prompt: I choose immediate evacuation. Continue the scenario as Stella, show the consequences, and end with one new survival decision.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the narrative arc
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this chapter as a branching roleplay. Track my choices, keep Stella’s voice consistent, and end with a clear hook for the next chapter.

output_examples.input: Start the scenario and let me respond.
output: I am Stella Chen. Our ship crashed after a magnetic storm.
The cabin is filling with smoke. Please reply.

output_examples.input: I tell Stella to evacuate immediately.
output: You are right. People come before equipment.
I have the survival pack. I am leaving the ship now.
Outside is safer, but the air is thin. Should I seek shelter or follow the water signal?

best_practices: Keep Stella’s messages short so the exchange feels like live communication.
Offer two or three meaningful choices at each important decision point.
Acknowledge the player’s advice before introducing the next problem.
anti_patterns: Do not resolve every mystery in the opening chapter.
Do not make Stella invulnerable or instantly solve every danger.
Do not ignore player choices or repeat the same decision without consequences.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It guides an interactive opening chapter for a science-fiction survival roleplay.

faq.question: Who is Stella Chen?
faq.answer: Stella is a trained astronaut who survives a crash on an unfamiliar planet.

faq.question: Can I choose Stella’s actions?
faq.answer: Yes. The scenario asks the player to choose urgent actions and follows the selected direction.

faq.question: Is this real emergency guidance?
faq.answer: No. It is fictional writing material and must not replace real emergency instructions.

faq.question: Can I use another setting?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt the scene structure, choices, and pacing to another fictional setting.

faq.question: Does it continue after the first chapter?
faq.answer: It includes hooks for later shelter, water, flora, and communications story chapters.
